analysis.title: Why buy Semis? (GS Malmstrom, 10 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Goldman's Jim Schneider argues the US semiconductor sell-off has gone too far. SOX is down more than 20% since October and the stocks are described as clearly oversold.
The sell-off followed the US elections on Nov 3. A Democratic sweep increased uncertainty about the pace of data center builds in states such as Texas.

Two tensions drove the drawdown. One is how the funding gap between current capex and free cash flow at hyperscalers and AI model labs gets closed. The other is whether enough land, power and shell capacity is coming online to match Street semiconductor estimates.

AI compute: GS favors NVDA and AVGO. At current prices they imply no growth from 2027. GS sees 35 GW of data center additions in 2027 as relatively low risk and treats its 2027 estimates as a solid base.
Even with no growth in 2028, which GS sees as relatively unlikely, NVDA and AVGO trade at 12X and 13X that baseline. GS calls these valuations compelling.
GS finds AMD very attractive on growth it expects, but at a less compelling valuation than NVDA and AVGO.
Semi cap equipment: GS treats 2027 wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX. Capacity coming online through 2028 is seen as catching up to past demand levels.
AMAT and LRCX trade at 15X and 16X 2027E EPS. GS calls them compelling even with no capex increase beyond 2027, which it views as highly unlikely.
Memory: GS says stocks are approaching oversold levels near tangible book value. Global memory stocks have historically bottomed around tangible book.
Samsung and SK Hynix (covered by Giuni Lee) are approaching those levels and now trade below total book value.
GS sees risk/reward becoming more attractive for Neutral-rated Micron because of strong free cash flow in coming quarters.
Aterio data compiled by GS: capacity under construction alone takes US data center capacity from 65GW-gross in 2026 to 143GW-gross by 2030. Net additions are 33/37/8/0GW-gross in 2027/28/29/30.
Adding announced capacity tagged high likelihood by Aterio would add 3/35/61/38GW-gross to 2027/28/29/30.
Under-construction capacity gives visibility into net additions through 2028. Announced but not yet under construction capacity is the key driver of 2028 upside and of 2029-30.
Texas alone makes up 26% of 2026-30 cumulative data center capacity net additions.

risk_factors: The funding gap between current capex and free cash flow at hyperscalers and AI model labs may not close.
Land, power and shell capacity may not come online fast enough to match Street semiconductor estimates.
Political uncertainty after the Democratic sweep may slow data center builds in states such as Texas.
Announced capacity not yet under construction carries higher risk and is the key driver of 2028 upside and of 2029-30.

tension_points.bull_case: GS says the sell-off has gone too far. NVDA, AVGO, AMAT and LRCX trade at compelling multiples against 2027 baselines, and 35 GW of 2027 data center additions carries low risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex exceeds free cash flow at hyperscalers and AI labs with no clear funding path. It is also unclear that land, power and shell capacity will arrive in line with Street semiconductor estimates. The election outcome adds uncertainty to Texas builds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capacity additions falling short of the 35 GW GS expects for 2027, or no increase in capex beyond 2027 (GS views the latter as highly unlikely).
